permit_only_areas.note: Aboriginal shire and Torres Strait council areas, where entry or camping needs a permit from the community or traditional owners. Every camp inside these council areas (QSpatial QPWS points and OpenStreetMap camps) is left out while include_permit_only_areas is false. Set permit_only_qpws_exempt to true to keep QPWS camps there and leave out only the others.

qpws_camps.note: QSpatial tourist points layer, feature_type Camping Ground, State of Queensland, CC BY 4.0. A point is kept as a QPWS camp when its attribute_source is the Queensland environment or national parks department, or it lies inside a QPWS park or state forest. Other points (council, water authority and private sites) are left to OpenStreetMap and council batches. The layer has no fee, facility or open status fields. Fetched when this state is built.

qpws_estates.note: QSpatial protected areas and state forests (estatename, esttype, qpwsreg), CC BY 4.0. Prepared into data/qpws-estates.json by scripts/fetch_qld_reference.py. Used to match park alerts to camps.

qpws_alerts_rss.note: QPWS park alerts RSS. Each item ends with 'Affected parks: …' and links to its alert page. A camp is marked closed only where the alert closes the whole park, or names that camping area as closed, and the closure has started. A later start is an upcoming notice. Other alerts are notes. Fetched when this state is built.

bom_fdr_qld.note: Bureau of Meteorology Fire Danger Ratings 4 Days (QLD), IDQ13016. The rating for today and tomorrow (Queensland local dates) is shown for the fire weather district that contains the camp. Fetched when this state is built with a browser user agent (BoM refuses script user agents). If the feed is unavailable, the line is omitted.

qld_fire_districts.note: Queensland fire weather districts (New_Fire_Districts), Public Safety Business Agency for the Queensland Fire Department, published with the QFD story map 'Queensland Fire Weather District changes 19 August'. DIST_NAME matches the IDQ13016 area description.

qldtraffic.public_key_source: https://qldtraffic.qld.gov.au/media/moreDevelopers-and-Data/qldtraffic-website-api-specification-v1-10.pdf (public API access key, globally limited to 100 requests/minute)
qldtraffic.note: QLDTraffic GeoJSON API v2 (Department of Transport and Main Roads), CC BY 4.0. Uses the registered key in the QLDTRAFFIC_API_KEY environment variable when set; otherwise TMR's published public key (delete public_key to skip instead). Flooding events and road closures within 5 km of a camp are listed on its page.

qpws_permits.note: QPWS camping permits CSV (data.qld.gov.au, CC BY 4.0). Park and camping area names only, used to cross-check camps.

abs_tourism_regions.note: ABS ASGS Edition 3 Tourism Regions 2021, Queensland only. CC BY 4.0. Prepared into data/qld-tourism-regions.json. A camp is grouped by the region that contains it.

qld_lgas.note: QSpatial Local Government areas, CC BY 4.0. Names the council area of each camp and drives the permit-only exclusion.

safety_html: Not an official warning service. A camp page can show the Bureau of Meteorology fire danger rating for that camp's Queensland fire weather district. Queensland declares local fire bans by area, and they are not copied here: check Queensland Fire Department fire bans and restrictions. It does not republish incident warnings. Always check the Queensland Fire Department, Queensland SES, QLDTraffic and the Bureau of Meteorology warnings for Queensland before you travel. In the wet season many northern and western roads and parks close. In an emergency call 000.

faq.q: Does the QSpatial camping layer say if a Queensland camp is open?
faq.a: No. The camping-ground points do not include open or closed status, fees or facilities. Fees and facilities stay blank. The site reads the QPWS park alerts RSS: a camp is marked closed only where an alert closes the whole park or names that camping area as closed, and the closure has started. A later start is an upcoming notice. Every other camp stays check. The camp page also shows its Queensland fire weather district fire danger rating from the Bureau of Meteorology.

faq.q: Why is there no Total Fire Ban line for Queensland camps?
faq.a: Queensland declares local fire bans by area rather than Total Fire Bans by district, and there is no official machine-readable feed to copy. Queensland camp pages show the Bureau of Meteorology fire danger rating and link to the Queensland Fire Department fire bans and restrictions page.

faq.q: Why are some Cape York, Gulf and Torres Strait camps missing?
faq.a: Camps in Aboriginal shire and Torres Strait council areas, where entry or camping needs a permit from the community or traditional owners, are not listed. Check with the council or land trust before you travel.
